title: Math.random() where strength may matter — review required
description: Math.random() is not cryptographically secure: its output is predictable once the seed state is known. Tokens, password-reset codes, or shuffle orders built on it can be guessed. This lexical rule flags every call; the reviewer decides whether the context needs crypto randomness.
remediation: Use crypto.getRandomValues() (browser) or crypto.randomBytes()/randomInt() (Node) for tokens, secrets, and security choices. Keep Math.random() only for non-security uses like games and sampling.
limitation: Lexical: cannot tell games from tokens, so safe uses match too. Review the dataflow: if the output guards anything, replace it.
